claim: Intermittent parathyroid hormone (iPTH) attenuates osteoarthritis pain by inhibiting subchondral sensory innervation, subchondral bone deterioration, and articular cartilage degeneration in a destabilized medial meniscus (DMM) mouse model.
source: Here, we show that intermittent parathyroid hormone (iPTH) attenuates osteoarthritis pain by inhibiting subchondral sensory innervation, subchondral bone deterioration, and articular cartilage degeneration in a destabilized medial meniscus (DMM) mouse model.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by multiple experimental results presented throughout the manuscript including pain behavior tests, histological analyses, and microCT data.

claim: Subchondral sensory innervation for osteoarthritis pain was significantly decreased in PTH-treated DMM mice compared with vehicle-treated DMM mice.
source: We found that subchondral sensory innervation for osteoarthritis pain was significantly decreased in PTH-treated DMM mice compared with vehicle-treated DMM mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced density of CGRP+ nerve fibers in subchondral bone of PTH-treated mice (Figure 2A,B).

claim: Deterioration of subchondral bone microarchitecture in DMM mice was attenuated by iPTH treatment.
source: In parallel, deterioration of subchondral bone microarchitecture in DMM mice was attenuated by iPTH treatment.
evidence: This is supported by microCT analysis showing improved structural parameters (Tb.pf, SMI, Po.V(tot), SBP.Th) in PTH-treated mice (Figure 3).

claim: Increased level of prostaglandin E2 in subchondral bone of DMM mice was reduced by iPTH treatment.
source: Increased level of prostaglandin E2 in subchondral bone of DMM mice was reduced by iPTH treatment.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA measurements showing reduced PGE2 levels in subchondral bone of PTH-treated DMM mice (Figure 2M).

claim: Uncoupled subchondral bone remodeling caused by increased transforming growth factor β signaling was regulated by PTH-induced endocytosis of the PTH type 1 receptor–transforming growth factor β type 2 receptor complex.
source: Furthermore, uncoupled subchondral bone remodeling caused by increased transforming growth factor β signaling was regulated by PTH-induced endocytosis of the PTH type 1 receptor–transforming growth factor β type 2 receptor complex.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing PTH-induced reduction in cell-surface TβRII and decreased pSmad2/3 signaling (Figure 4J,K).

claim: iPTH improved subchondral bone microarchitecture and decreased level of prostaglandin E2 and sensory innervation of subchondral bone in DMM mice by acting specifically through PTH type 1 receptor in Nestin+ mesenchymal stromal cells.
source: Notably, iPTH improved subchondral bone microarchitecture and decreased level of prostaglandin E2 and sensory innervation of subchondral bone in DMM mice by acting specifically through PTH type 1 receptor in Nestin+ mesenchymal stromal cells.
evidence: This is supported by conditional knockout experiments showing that deletion of PTH1R in Nestin+ MSCs abolished the effects of iPTH on pain, sensory innervation, PGE2 levels, and bone microarchitecture (Figures 6 and 7).

claim: Osteoarthritis is the most common degenerative joint disorder in the USA and a leading cause of disability.
source: Osteoarthritis is the most common degenerative joint disorder in the USA and a leading cause of disability (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), 2009; Murray et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to CDC and Murray et al. publications.

claim: Chronic pain affects nearly 40 million people in the USA with osteoarthritis.
source: Chronic pain is a prominent symptom of osteoarthritis, affecting nearly 40 million people in the USA (Peat et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Peat et al. 2001.

claim: Pain itself is a major risk factor for the development of functional limitation and disability in patients with osteoarthritis.
source: Pain itself is also a major risk factor for the development of functional limitation and disability in patients with osteoarthritis (Lane et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lane et al. 2010.

claim: Available therapies (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, analgesics, and steroids) do not provide sustained pain relief and can have substantial adverse effects.
source: Available therapies (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, analgesics, and steroids) do not provide sustained pain relief and can have substantial adverse effects (Geba et al., 2002; Karlsson et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Geba et al. 2002 and Karlsson et al. 2002.

claim: Inadequate control of chronic osteoarthritis pain is a major reason that patients seek surgical treatment.
source: Inadequate control of chronic osteoarthritis pain is a major reason that patients seek surgical treatment.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction without specific citation.

claim: Osteoarthritis pain can manifest during very early stages of the disease, in the absence of synovial inflammation and independently of progressive cartilage degeneration.
source: Yet, osteoarthritis pain can manifest during very early stages of the disease, in the absence of synovial inflammation and independently of progressive cartilage degeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Many patients have radiographic osteoarthritic changes but no symptoms, whereas others have osteoarthritis pain with no radiographic indications.
source: Many patients have radiographic osteoarthritic changes but no symptoms, whereas others have osteoarthritis pain with no radiographic indications (Dieppe and Lohmander, 2005; Hannan et al., 2000; Bedson and Croft, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dieppe and Lohmander 2005, Hannan et al. 2000, and Bedson and Croft 2008.

claim: Some patients have bilateral radiographic evidence of knee osteoarthritis yet have unilateral knee pain.
source: Some patients have bilateral radiographic evidence of knee osteoarthritis yet have unilateral knee pain.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical observation.

claim: Subchondral bone marrow edema–like lesions are highly correlated with osteoarthritis pain.
source: Intriguingly, subchondral bone marrow edema–like lesions are highly correlated with osteoarthritis pain (Yusuf et al., 2011; Kwoh, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yusuf et al. 2011 and Kwoh 2013.

claim: Zoledronic acid, which inhibits osteoclast activity, reduces the size of bone marrow edema–like lesions and concomitantly alleviates pain.
source: Zoledronic acid, which inhibits osteoclast activity, reduces the size of bone marrow edema–like lesions and concomitantly alleviates pain (Laslett et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Laslett et al. 2012.

claim: Patients taking bisphosphonates experienced significantly reduced knee pain at years 2 and 3 according to data from the National Institutes of Health Osteoarthritis Initiative.
source: Analysis of data from the National Institutes of Health Osteoarthritis Initiative reported that patients taking bisphosphonates experienced significantly reduced knee pain at years 2 and 3 (Laslett et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Laslett et al. 2014.

claim: Patients with osteoarthritis report rapid and obvious pain relief after removal of deteriorated subchondral bone with overlying cartilage through knee replacement.
source: Furthermore, patients with osteoarthritis report rapid and obvious pain relief after removal of deteriorated subchondral bone with overlying cartilage through knee replacement (Isaac et al., 2005; Reilly et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Isaac et al. 2005 and Reilly et al. 2005.

claim: Articular cartilage is characteristically aneural and avascular.
source: Articular cartilage, which is characteristically aneural and avascular (Bhosale and Richardson, 2008), is incapable of generating pain primarily, suggesting that subchondral bone is a major source of osteoarthritis pain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bhosale and Richardson 2008.

claim: Articular cartilage is incapable of generating pain primarily, suggesting that subchondral bone is a major source of osteoarthritis pain.
source: Articular cartilage, which is characteristically aneural and avascular (Bhosale and Richardson, 2008), is incapable of generating pain primarily, suggesting that subchondral bone is a major source of osteoarthritis pain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the aneural nature of cartilage and clinical observations.

claim: Aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is a critical factor in pathological changes of osteoarthritis.
source: Aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is a critical factor in pathological changes of osteoarthritis (Zhen and Cao, 2014; Zhen et al., 2013), and sensory innervation induced by netrin-1 from aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is responsible for osteoarthritis pain (Zhu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhen and Cao 2014 and Zhen et al. 2013.

claim: Sensory innervation induced by netrin-1 from aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is responsible for osteoarthritis pain.
source: Aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is a critical factor in pathological changes of osteoarthritis (Zhen and Cao, 2014; Zhen et al., 2013), and sensory innervation induced by netrin-1 from aberrant subchondral bone remodeling is responsible for osteoarthritis pain (Zhu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhu et al. 2019.

claim: Locally elevated levels of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) activate sensory nerves in porous endplates, leading to sodium influx through Nav1.8 channels, to mediate spinal hypersensitivity.
source: Furthermore, locally elevated levels of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) activate sensory nerves in porous endplates, leading to sodium influx through Nav1.8 channels, to mediate spinal hypersensitivity (Ni et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ni et al. 2019.

claim: Bone homeostasis is maintained by temporal-spatial activation of transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) to couple bone resorption and formation.
source: We have shown that bone homeostasis is maintained by temporal-spatial activation of transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) to couple bone resorption and formation (Tang et al., 2009), in which subchondral bone is maintained in a native microarchitecture with blood vessels and nerves intertwined under normal conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tang et al. 2009.

claim: Excessive active TGF-β in the subchondral bone induces aberrant bone remodeling at the onset of osteoarthritis to promote its progression.
source: However, excessive active TGF-β in the subchondral bone induces aberrant bone remodeling at the onset of osteoarthritis to promote its progression (Zhen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhen et al. 2013.

claim: High levels of active TGF-β recruit mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and osteoprogenitors in clusters, leading to abnormal bone formation and angiogenesis.
source: Specifically, high levels of active TGF-β recruit mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and osteoprogenitors in clusters, leading to abnormal bone formation and angiogenesis (Zhen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhen et al. 2013.

claim: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a U.S. Food and Drug Administration–approved anabolic agent for osteoporosis that regulates bone remodeling and calcium metabolism.
source: Parathyroid hormone (PTH), a U.S. Food and Drug Administration–approved anabolic agent for osteoporosis, regulates bone remodeling and calcium metabolism (Crane and Cao, 2014; Qiu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Crane and Cao 2014 and Qiu et al. 2010.

claim: The parathyroid gland evolved in amphibians and supported the transition from aquatic to terrestrial life, allowing terrestrial locomotion in previously aquatic vertebrates.
source: The parathyroid gland, the main production site of PTH, evolved in amphibians and supported the transition from aquatic to terrestrial life, allowing terrestrial locomotion in previously aquatic vertebrates (Okabe and Graham, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Okabe and Graham 2004.

claim: PTH prevents cartilage degeneration and/or the deterioration of subchondral bone.
source: PTH prevents cartilage degeneration and/or the deterioration of subchondral bone (Sampson et al., 2011; Orth et al., 2013; Bellido et al., 2011; Yan et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2009; Lugo et al., 2012; Eswaramoorthy et al., 2012; Cui et al., 2020; Morita et al., 2018; Dai et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2018), induces cartilage regeneration or chondrocytes proliferation in osteoarthritis (Sampson et al., 2011; Petersson et al., 2006), and stimulates subchondral bone and articular cartilage repair of focal osteochondral defects (Orth et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: PTH induces cartilage regeneration or chondrocytes proliferation in osteoarthritis.
source: PTH prevents cartilage degeneration and/or the deterioration of subchondral bone (Sampson et al., 2011; Orth et al., 2013; Bellido et al., 2011; Yan et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2009; Lugo et al., 2012; Eswaramoorthy et al., 2012; Cui et al., 2020; Morita et al., 2018; Dai et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2018), induces cartilage regeneration or chondrocytes proliferation in osteoarthritis (Sampson et al., 2011; Petersson et al., 2006), and stimulates subchondral bone and articular cartilage repair of focal osteochondral defects (Orth et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sampson et al. 2011 and Petersson et al. 2006.

claim: PTH stimulates subchondral bone and articular cartilage repair of focal osteochondral defects.
source: PTH prevents cartilage degeneration and/or the deterioration of subchondral bone (Sampson et al., 2011; Orth et al., 2013; Bellido et al., 2011; Yan et al., 2014; Chang et al., 2009; Lugo et al., 2012; Eswaramoorthy et al., 2012; Cui et al., 2020; Morita et al., 2018; Dai et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2018), induces cartilage regeneration or chondrocytes proliferation in osteoarthritis (Sampson et al., 2011; Petersson et al., 2006), and stimulates subchondral bone and articular cartilage repair of focal osteochondral defects (Orth et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Orth et al. 2013.

claim: PTH interacts with local osteotropic factors to orchestrate the coupling of bone resorption and formation in an anabolic signaling network.
source: PTH also interacts with local osteotropic factors to orchestrate the coupling of bone resorption and formation in an anabolic signaling network (Qiu et al., 2010; Pfeilschifter et al., 1995), and PTH and TGF-β work in concert to exert their physiological activities in bone (Qiu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Qiu et al. 2010 and Pfeilschifter et al. 1995.

claim: PTH and TGF-β work in concert to exert their physiological activities in bone.
source: PTH also interacts with local osteotropic factors to orchestrate the coupling of bone resorption and formation in an anabolic signaling network (Qiu et al., 2010; Pfeilschifter et al., 1995), and PTH and TGF-β work in concert to exert their physiological activities in bone (Qiu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Qiu et al. 2010.

claim: TGF-β elicits its cellular response through the ligand-induced formation of a heteromeric complex containing TGF-β types 1 (TβRI) and 2 (TβRII) kinase receptors.
source: TGF-β elicits its cellular response through the ligand-induced formation of a heteromeric complex containing TGF-β types 1 (TβRI) and 2 (TβRII) kinase receptors (Tang et al., 2009; Wrana et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tang et al. 2009 and Wrana et al. 1992.

claim: PTH induces endocytosis of PTH type one receptor (PTH1R) with TβRII as a complex, and both PTH and TGF-β signaling are co-regulated during endocytosis.
source: We have shown that PTH induces endocytosis of PTH type one receptor (PTH1R) with TβRII as a complex, and both PTH and TGF-β signaling are co-regulated during endocytosis (Qiu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Qiu et al. 2010.

claim: The 50% PWT of sham mice returned to baseline by week 3 after surgery, indicating that secondary hyperalgesia during the first 2 weeks is attributable to surgery alone.
source: The 50% PWT of sham mice returned to baseline by week 3 after surgery, indicating that secondary hyperalgesia during the first 2 weeks is attributable to surgery alone.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that sham-operated mice recovered to baseline, suggesting the initial pain was due to surgical trauma.

claim: The 50% PWT of vehicle mice continued to worsen from week 2 onward, but the 50% PWT of PTH mice stabilized at levels significantly higher than those of vehicle mice.
source: The 50% PWT of vehicle mice continued to worsen from week 2 onward, but the 50% PWT of PTH mice stabilized at levels significantly higher than those of vehicle mice (Figure 1A), indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis reduced secondary hyperalgesia.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis reduced secondary hyperalgesia.
source: The 50% PWT of vehicle mice continued to worsen from week 2 onward, but the 50% PWT of PTH mice stabilized at levels significantly higher than those of vehicle mice (Figure 1A), indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis reduced secondary hyperalgesia.
evidence: This is an inference based on the 50% PWT data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: PAMWT of sham mice recovered to near-baseline by week 4.
source: PAMWT of sham mice recovered to near-baseline by week 4.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PAM withdrawal threshold of vehicle mice improved by week 4, albeit to a lesser extent compared with sham mice, and gradually declined between weeks 4 and 8.
source: PAM withdrawal threshold of vehicle mice also improved by week 4, albeit to a lesser extent compared with sham mice, and gradually declined between weeks 4 and 8.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PAMWT of PTH mice was significantly higher than that of vehicle mice at every time point between week 2 and week 8 after surgery, indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis reduced primary hyperalgesia.
source: PAMWT of PTH mice and vehicle mice changed in a similar pattern over time; however, the PAMWT of PTH mice was significantly higher than that of vehicle mice at every time point between week 2 and week 8 after surgery (Figure 1B), indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis reduced primary hyperalgesia.
evidence: This is based on data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At week 8 after DMM surgery, the affected hind paw intensity, contact area, and swing speed decreased significantly relative to contralateral hind paws; however, these differences were less pronounced in PTH mice.
source: At week 8 after DMM surgery (compared with sham surgery), the affected hind paw intensity, contact area, and swing speed decreased significantly relative to contralateral hind paws; however, these differences were less pronounced in PTH mice (Figure 1D), indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis improved gait deficits.
evidence: This is based on gait analysis data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis improved gait deficits.
source: At week 8 after DMM surgery (compared with sham surgery), the affected hind paw intensity, contact area, and swing speed decreased significantly relative to contralateral hind paws; however, these differences were less pronounced in PTH mice (Figure 1D), indicating that iPTH initiated early in the development of osteoarthritis improved gait deficits.
evidence: This is an inference based on gait analysis data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: OARSI score increased progressively in DMM mice over 8 weeks, but this progression was reduced and slower in PTH mice.
source: OARSI score increased progressively in DMM mice over 8 weeks, but this progression was reduced and slower in PTH mice (Figure 1F), indicating that early initiation of iPTH in osteoarthritis slowed the progression of articular cartilage degeneration.
evidence: This is based on OARSI scoring data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH in osteoarthritis slowed the progression of articular cartilage degeneration.
source: OARSI score increased progressively in DMM mice over 8 weeks, but this progression was reduced and slower in PTH mice (Figure 1F), indicating that early initiation of iPTH in osteoarthritis slowed the progression of articular cartilage degeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on OARSI scoring data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Percentages of ColX+ and MMP13+ chondrocytes more than doubled in DMM mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH significantly reduced the magnitude of increase.
source: Percentages of ColX+ and MMP13+ chondrocytes more than doubled in DMM mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH significantly reduced the magnitude of increase (Figure 1H), indicating that iPTH inhibited chondrocyte degeneration in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: iPTH inhibited chondrocyte degeneration in osteoarthritis.
source: Percentages of ColX+ and MMP13+ chondrocytes more than doubled in DMM mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH significantly reduced the magnitude of increase (Figure 1H), indicating that iPTH inhibited chondrocyte degeneration in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is an inference based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: The density of CGRP+ nerve endings increased significantly after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery.
source: The density of CGRP+ nerve endings increased significantly after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Although the density of CGRP+ sensory nerve fibers also increased in PTH mice, the effect was significantly diminished relative to vehicle mice, indicating that iPTH inhibited the growth of nociceptive nerve fibers in osteoarthritic subchondral bone.
source: Although the density of CGRP+ sensory nerve fibers also increased in PTH mice, the effect was significantly diminished relative to vehicle mice, indicating that iPTH inhibited the growth of nociceptive nerve fibers in osteoarthritic subchondral bone.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The density of SP+, P2 × 3+, and PIEZO2+ nociceptive fibers increased in the subchondral bone of vehicle mice compared with sham mice, whereas iPTH treatment attenuated the increase of these nociceptive innervations.
source: The density of SP+, P2 × 3+, and PIEZO2+ nociceptive fibers also increased in the subchondral bone of vehicle mice compared with sham mice, whereas iPTH treatment attenuated the increase of these nociceptive innervations (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The density of EMUN + vessels increased in subchondral bone of vehicle mice compared with sham mice, while iPTH treatment attenuated the increase in these vessels.
source: Like CGRP+ nerve fibers, the density of EMUN + vessels increased in subchondral bone of vehicle mice compared with sham mice, while iPTH treatment attenuated the increase in these vessels (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence co-staining shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: The density of CGRP+ sensory nerve endings increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery in synovium, and iPTH treatment had no influence on this effect.
source: The density of CGRP+ sensory nerve endings increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, and iPTH treatment had no influence on this effect (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence analysis of synovium shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: iPTH reduces osteoarthritis pain by specific inhibition of sensory nerve innervation in subchondral bone.
source: Together, these findings suggest that iPTH reduces osteoarthritis pain by specific inhibition of sensory nerve innervation in subchondral bone.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of iPTH on sensory innervation in subchondral bone versus synovium.

claim: There was no significant difference in osteophyte volume between PTH and vehicle-treated DMM mice, despite both are significantly higher than sham group.
source: There was no significant difference in osteophyte volume between PTH and vehicle-treated DMM mice, despite both are significantly higher than sham group (Figure 2I,J).
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 2I,J.

claim: The number of COX2+ cell increased significantly after DMM surgery in vehicle mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH diminished this increase.
source: The number of COX2+ cell increased significantly after DMM surgery in vehicle mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH diminished this increase (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 2K,L.

claim: The level of PGE2 increased after DMM surgery in vehicle mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH inhibited this effect.
source: The level of PGE2 also increased after DMM surgery in vehicle mice compared with sham mice, and iPTH inhibited this effect (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is based on ELISA measurements shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH reduced the level of PGE2 in osteoarthritis subchondral bone.
source: These results indicate that early initiation of iPTH reduced the level of PGE2 in osteoarthritis subchondral bone.
evidence: This is an inference based on COX2 and PGE2 measurements.

claim: Trabecular bone pattern factor (Tb.pf) increased rapidly by week 4 and plateaued in vehicle mice after DMM surgery, indicating uncoupled subchondral bone remodeling.
source: Trabecular bone pattern factor (Tb.pf), a measure of disruption in trabecular bone connectivity (Hahn et al., 1992), increased rapidly by week 4 and plateaued in vehicle mice after DMM surgery (Figure 3B), indicating uncoupled subchondral bone remodeling.
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3B, with inference about uncoupled remodeling.

claim: Tb.Pf in PTH mice after DMM surgery was no different from sham mice within 2 weeks postoperatively, but increased by week 8. However, Tb.Pf of PTH mice was significantly lower than that of vehicle mice.
source: Tb.Pf in PTH mice after DMM surgery was no different from sham mice within 2 weeks postoperatively, but increased by week 8. However, Tb.Pf of PTH mice was significantly lower than that of vehicle mice (Figure 3B), which indicates that early initiation of iPTH slowed the disruption of subchondral trabecular bone connectivity in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH slowed the disruption of subchondral trabecular bone connectivity in osteoarthritis.
source: Tb.Pf in PTH mice after DMM surgery was no different from sham mice within 2 weeks postoperatively, but increased by week 8. However, Tb.Pf of PTH mice was significantly lower than that of vehicle mice (Figure 3B), which indicates that early initiation of iPTH slowed the disruption of subchondral trabecular bone connectivity in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is an inference based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Structure model index (SMI) increased significantly by week 4 and was sustained in vehicle mice at week 8 after DMM surgery, indicating a change from plate-predominant to rod-predominant cancellous bone architecture in the development of osteoarthritis.
source: Structure model index (SMI), a measure to quantify the architectural type of cancellous bone (Hildebrand and Rüegsegger, 1997), increased significantly by week 4. This increase was sustained in vehicle mice at week 8 after DMM surgery (Figure 3C), indicating a change from plate-predominant to rod-predominant cancellous bone architecture in the development of osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3C, with inference about architectural changes.

claim: SMI in PTH mice increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, but the magnitude of increase was less than that of vehicle mice at every time point, indicating that early initiation of iPTH slowed the architectural deterioration of subchondral bone in osteoarthritis.
source: SMI in PTH mice also increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, but the magnitude of increase was less than that of vehicle mice at every time point (Figure 3C). This difference indicates that early initiation of iPTH slowed the architectural deterioration of subchondral bone in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Total volume of pore space (Po.V(tot)) and subchondral bone plate thickness (SBP.Th) increased gradually in vehicle mice and PTH mice after DMM surgery compared with sham mice, but the magnitudes of increase in PTH mice were significantly lower than those in vehicle mice at every time point.
source: Total volume of pore space (Po.V(tot)) and subchondral bone plate thickness (SBP.Th) increased gradually in vehicle mice and PTH mice after DMM surgery compared with sham mice, but the magnitudes of increase in PTH mice were significantly lower than those in vehicle mice at every time point (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is based on μCT analysis shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH slowed the deterioration and hypertrophy of subchondral bone microarchitecture in osteoarthritis.
source: These results indicate that early initiation of iPTH slowed the deterioration and hypertrophy of subchondral bone microarchitecture in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is an inference based on μCT analysis of multiple structural parameters.

claim: Trichrome staining showed that osteoids formed islets in the subchondral bone marrow of DMM mice.
source: Trichrome staining showed that osteoids formed islets in the subchondral bone marrow of DMM mice.
evidence: This is based on trichrome staining shown in Figure 3F.

claim: iPTH induced formation of osteoids on subchondral bone surface in DMM mice, similar to sham mice.
source: iPTH induced formation of osteoids on subchondral bone surface in DMM mice, similar to sham mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on trichrome staining shown in Figure 3F.

claim: iPTH plays an essential role in sustaining coupled subchondral bone remodeling in osteoarthritis.
source: These results suggest that iPTH plays an essential role in sustaining coupled subchondral bone remodeling in osteoarthritis.
evidence: This is an inference based on trichrome staining and fluorescent double-labeling experiments.

claim: The number of Nestin+ cells in the subchondral bone marrow was significantly higher in vehicle mice compared with sham mice.
source: Immunostaining for Nestin, a marker for adult bone marrow MSCs, showed a significantly higher number of Nestin+ cells in the subchondral bone marrow of vehicle mice compared with sham mice (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on immunostaining shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The number of Osterix+ osteoprogenitors was greater in the subchondral bone marrow of vehicle mice compared with sham mice.
source: The number of Osterix+ osteoprogenitors was also greater in the subchondral bone marrow of vehicle mice compared with sham mice (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Intermittent PTH attenuated the increases of Nestin+ and Osterix+ cells in subchondral bone marrow of DMM mice.
source: Intermittent PTH attenuated the increases of Nestin+ and Osterix+ cells in subchondral bone marrow of DMM mice (Figure 4A–D), suggesting that early initiation of iPTH attenuates aberrant bone formation in osteoarthritis by modulating the recruitment of osteoprogenitors in subchondral bone.
evidence: This is based on immunostaining shown in Figure 4A-D.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH attenuates aberrant bone formation in osteoarthritis by modulating the recruitment of osteoprogenitors in subchondral bone.
source: Intermittent PTH attenuated the increases of Nestin+ and Osterix+ cells in subchondral bone marrow of DMM mice (Figure 4A–D), suggesting that early initiation of iPTH attenuates aberrant bone formation in osteoarthritis by modulating the recruitment of osteoprogenitors in subchondral bone.
evidence: This is an inference based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A-D.

claim: The number of pSmad2/3+ cells in subchondral bone increased significantly after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, but this effect was significantly attenuated in PTH mice.
source: Immunostaining of pSmad2/3 revealed that the number of pSmad2/3+ cells in subchondral bone increased significantly after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, but this effect was significantly attenuated in PTH mice (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 4E,F.

claim: The number of osteoclasts increased significantly in subchondral bone 4 weeks post-DMM surgery; interestingly, iPTH treatment further increased the number of TRAP+ osteoclasts in subchondral bone.
source: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase+ (TRAP+) staining showed that the number of osteoclasts increased significantly in subchondral bone 4 weeks post-DMM surgery; interestingly, iPTH treatment further increased the number of TRAP+ osteoclasts in subchondral bone (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is based on TRAP staining shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: Active TGF-β1 concentration increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, and iPTH further increased the active TGF-β1 concentration in DMM mice compared with vehicle mice.
source: Furthermore, ELISA of active TGF-β1 in serum revealed that active TGF-β1 concentration increased after DMM surgery compared with sham surgery, and iPTH further increased the active TGF-β1 concentration in DMM mice compared with vehicle mice (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is based on ELISA measurements shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Early initiation of iPTH attenuates aberrant subchondral bone remodeling by interfering with downstream TGF-β signaling in osteoarthritis.
